correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the complete equality chain. From tr(S)=n and nonnegative eigenvalues, Cauchy-Schwarz gives tr(S^2)>=n^2/d. The rank-one expansion gives tr(S^2)=n+sum_{j!=k}a_jk a_kj, and the correlation bound gives tr(S^2)-n<=sum|a_jk a_kj|<=n(n-1)M^2. At M^2=(n-d)/(d(n-1)), the endpoints coincide, so all eigenvalues are n/d and every ordered product has modulus M^2. Diagonalizability then gives S=(n/d)I, while |a_jk|,|a_kj|<=M force every off-diagonal modulus to equal M. The n=d boundary has M=0 and is included.
